segments.text:
I.
HOW fine has the Day been, how
bright was the Sun,
How lovely and joyful the Courſe that he run,
Tho' he roſe in a Miſt when his Race he
begun,
And there follow'd ſome Droppings of
Rain!
But now the fair Traveller's come to the Weſt,
His Rays are all Gold, and his Beauties
are beſt;
He paints the Sky gay as he ſinks to his
Reſt,
And foretels a bright Riſing again.

II.
Juſt ſuch is the Chriſtian: His Courſe he
begins,
Like the Sun in a Miſt, while he mourns
for his Sins,
And melts into Tears: Then he breaks
out and ſhines,
And travels his heav'nly Way:
But when he comes nearer to finiſh his Race,
Like a fine ſetting Sun he looks richer in
Grace,
And gives a ſure Hope at the End of his Days
Of riſing in brighter Array.
